akhfash:3-3.t: His words ﴿مِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ﴾: you say "غَسَقَ" "يَغْسِقُ" "غُسُوقاً", and it is "darkness" (الظلمة). And "وَقَب" "يَقِبُ" "وُقُوباً", which is entering into a thing.

celaleyn:1-1.t: This sūra and the one after it were revealed when Labīd the Jew bewitched the Prophet ﷺ by means of a bowstring with eleven knots in it. Allah informed him of that and of its location, so it was brought before him ﷺ, and he was commanded to seek refuge with the two sūras. Whenever he recited a verse of them a knot came undone and he felt lighter, until all the knots came undone and he rose as though released from a hobble. ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ﴾: the daybreak,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ﴾, of living beings, accountable and non-accountable, and inanimate things such as poison and other things,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ﴾, that is, the night when it grows dark, or the moon when it disappears,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ﴾: the sorceresses who blow ﴿فِي الْعُقَدِ﴾ that they tie in the thread, blowing on them with something they say, without spittle; al-Zamakhsharī said: with it — such as the daughters of the aforementioned Labīd,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ﴾, that is, shows his envy and acts according to what it requires, like the aforementioned Labīd, of the Jews who envied the Prophet ﷺ. The mention of the three, which «ما خلق» already includes, after it, is because of the intensity of their evil.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿أَعُوذُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِرَبِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْفَلَقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿مِنْ شَرِّ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعوذ. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ﴾ the two are conjoined (maʿṭūfān) to what precedes them. ﴿غاسِقٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿وَقَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثاتِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فِي الْعُقَدِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَمِنْ شَرِّ حاسِدٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿حَسَدَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

farraa:1-1.t:
[151/b] His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ﴾.
«الفلق» is the dawn; one says: it is clearer than the break (فلق) of dawn, and the parting (فرق) of dawn. The Prophet ﷺ had fallen gravely ill, and one day, as he was between sleep and waking, two angels came to him. One of them said: What is his ailment? The other said: He has a spell (طبّ) [placed] in a well, under a rock in it. The Prophet ﷺ woke up and sent ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir with a group of men to the well, and he brought out the sorcery. It was a bowstring with eleven knots in it; and whenever they untied a knot, he found relief, until the knots were untied, and it was as if he had been released from a tether. He was commanded to seek refuge with these two surahs, which are eleven verses, the number of the knots. The one who bewitched him was Labīd ibn Aʿṣam.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ﴾.
«الغاسق» is the night. "إذا وقب": when it enters into everything and grows dark. One says: غسق and أغسق.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي ٱلْعُقَدِ﴾.
They are the sorceresses who blow their sorcery. «ومِنْ شَرِّ حاسدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ»: meaning Labīd, who bewitched him.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «ما»: a nominal relative, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أَعُوذُ}, i.e.: I seek refuge in Allah from this at such a time.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The preposition «في العقد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «النفاثات».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (من شر ما خلق): (ما) has the meaning of (الذي), and the pronoun is omitted from the ṣila (relative clause). That indicates that Allah, exalted be His mention, is the Creator of everything. Likewise, if you make (ما) together with the verb a maṣdar (verbal noun), it indicates that, except that there is then no omitted pronoun in the speech.
Whoever read «من شرٍّ» with tanwīn has deviated and altered the wording and the meaning, because he makes (ما) a negation and puts (من) before it — in his view it is attached to (خلق) — thus putting what comes after the negation before it, and that is not permissible according to all the grammarians; for its implied form in his view is «ما خلق من شر» (He did not create any evil). So the speech departs from its bounds and turns into negation: after being a supplication and a seeking of refuge, it becomes a negative statement interposed between two seekings of refuge. That is clear deviation and an evident error.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت". The clause ﴿قل﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.
﴿أعوذ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا". The clause ﴿أعوذ﴾ is in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿برب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and رب is muḍāf.
﴿الفلق﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿من شر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and شر is muḍāf.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "from the evil of that which He created". Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "from the evil of His creation".
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to ﴿رب الناس﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; in this surah the phrase is ﴿رب الفلق﴾ (113:1) — ﴿رب الناس﴾ belongs to the next surah (114:1)]. The clause ﴿خلق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾ and has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ومن شر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction [joining this] to what preceded; ومن شر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and شر is muḍāf.
﴿غاسق﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿وقب﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to ﴿غاسق﴾. The clause ﴿وقب﴾ is in the position of the genitive because إذا is put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿ومن شر النفاثات﴾: the wāw is a conjunction [joining this] to what preceded; ومن شر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and شر is muḍāf.
﴿النفاثات﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿في العقد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿النفاثات﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ومن شر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction [joining this] to what preceded; ومن شر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعوذ﴾; and شر is muḍāf.
﴿حاسد﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿حسد﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to ﴿حاسد﴾. The clause ﴿حسد﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, ﴿إذا﴾ being put in construct with it.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
The scholars have differed over its meaning. Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: it is the dawn (al-ṣubḥ). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī said: it is Jahannam. It has also been said: it is creation; and it has been said: it is a valley in Jahannam. Abū Jaʿfar said:
When disagreement arises, one must return to the language in which the Quran was revealed, and the Arabs say: "It is clearer than the فلق of the morning and its فرق," meaning the daybreak (al-fajr).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ما may be a maṣdar (verbal-noun particle), in which case it needs no ʿāʾid (resumptive pronoun); and it may mean الذي (that which), in which case the hāʾ referring back to it is omitted.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The scholars have discussed the meaning of الغاسق. From the Prophet ﷺ [it is reported] that it is the moon, and we have mentioned that with its isnad. ʿUqayl narrated from al-Zuhrī, who said: «الغاسق إذا وقب» is the sun when it sets. Abū Jaʿfar said: Most of the exegetes hold that الغاسق is the night, and some of them said: the stars. If one returns to the language, one learns from it that one says غسق when it grows dark; so the views agree, because when the sun sets the night enters, the moon is [seen] at night, and the stars hardly appear except at night. So the meaning becomes: "and from the evil of the night when it enters with its darkness and covers everything." One says وقب when it enters; as for Qatāda's statement "وقب: it went away," it is not known [in the language].

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: [النفاثات is the] plural of نفّاثة, and in the broken plural نوافث. It is said that they were sorceresses in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; he commanded seeking refuge from them because they give the impression that they can benefit or harm, and so a person might incur in his religion something by which he sins. As for sorcery itself, it is false (bāṭil).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
Ibn Zayd said: they are the Jews. Someone else said: he is Labīd ibn Aʿṣam, and his daughters are the sorceresses.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most fitting of what has been said about this is the view of Qatāda, who said: it is for everyone who.... ] ... «[Translator's note: the source text is defective/truncated at this point; it is translated as it stands.]»

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {الفلق}: it is the daybreak. It is faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, like al-qabaḍ, i.e. that which is split open (maflūq). In the ḥadīth: "The vision [would come] like the breaking (falaq) of dawn." The poet said:
4682 - يا ليلةً لم أَنَمْها بِتُّ مُرْتَقِباً ... أَرْعَى النجومَ إلى أنْ نَوَّرَ الفَلَقُ
(O night in which I did not sleep! I spent it watchful, tending the stars until the daybreak shone.)
Dhū al-Rumma said:
4683 - حتى إذا ما انجلى عن وَجْهِه فَلَقٌ ... هادِيْهِ في أُخْرَياتِ الليلِ مُنْتَصِبُ
(Until, when a daybreak cleared from his face, his neck upraised in the last parts of the night…)
It was also said: it is a pit in Hell. It was also said: low-lying ground, whose plural is fulqān. It was also said: everything that is split, like the grain, and the earth [split] by the plants.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ}: attached to «أعوذُ». The generality read «شَرِّ» in construct with «ما»; ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read it with tanwīn. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and some of the Muʿtazila who hold that Allah did not create evil [read]: «مِنْ شَرٍّ» with tanwīn, «ما خلقَ» as a negation; it is a rejected reading built on a false doctrine." — end of quote. It is not necessary that «ما» be negative; rather it may be a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from «شر» with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "from evil — the evil of what He created": He made it general first [then specific second]. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "On this [reading] «ما» is a badal from «شرّ», or redundant (zāʾida). It is not permissible for it to be negative, because what lies within the domain of the negative [ما] does not precede it; therefore the implied form cannot be 'He did not create any evil'; moreover it is corrupt in meaning." I say: this is a fine technical rebuttal. And it may not be said that «مِنْ شرّ» is attached to «أعوذُ» and the object of «خَلَق» is omitted, because that is contrary to the norm. Makkī came down hard on the one who said this, and rejected him, with what was mentioned, in the harshest way. [And «ما» is maṣdariyya, or in the sense of «الذي».]

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {وَقَبَ}: "waqaba al-layl": the night grew dark; "[waqaba] the punishment": it descended; "[waqabat] the sun": [it set. It was also said: waqaba, i.e. it entered.] The poet said:
4684 - وَقَبَ العذابُ عليهمُ فكأنَّهمْ ... لَحِقَتْهُمُ نارُ الس‍َّمومِ فأُحْصِدوا
(The punishment descended upon them, and it was as though the fire of the scorching wind overtook them and they were mown down.)
Al-ghāsiq: it was said: the night; it was said: the moon. The night was called ghāsiq because of its coldness. Discussion of this root was given in Sūrat Ṣād. Refuge was sought from the night because of the harms that come by night in it. The poet said:
4685 - يا طيفَ هندٍ لقد أَبْقَيْتَ لي أَرَقا ... إذ جِئْتَنا طارقاً والليلُ قد غَسَقا
(O phantom of Hind, you have left me sleepless, when you came to us by night as the night grew dark.)
i.e. it grew dark and dense. «إذا» is accusative by «أعوذُ», i.e. "I seek refuge in Allah from this at such a time".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {النفاثات}: the plural of naffātha, an intensive form, from nafatha, i.e. he blew. There is disagreement about it. Abū al-Faḍl said: [it is] something like blowing from the mouth in incantation (ruqya), with nothing accompanying it; if it is with saliva, it is al-tafl (spitting). And he recited:
4686 - فإنْ يَبْرَأْ فلم أَنْفُِثْ عليهِ ... وإنْ يَفْقَدْ فَحَقَّ له الفُقُودُ
(If he recovers, it was not that I blew [incantations] upon him; and if he is lost, then loss was his due.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Blowing accompanied by saliva." Al-Ḥasan read «النُّفَّاثات» with ḍamma on the nūn; it is a noun, like al-nuffākha. Yaʿqūb and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim read «النافِثات», which admits [the same senses as] the reading of the generality. Al-Ḥasan also, and Abū al-Rabīʿ, read «النَّفِثات» without alif, like ḥādhir and ḥadhir. He made «غاسق» and «حاسد» indefinite because harm may fail to occur from them, so the indefiniteness conveys partitiveness. He made «النفَّاثات» definite either for a known reference (ʿahd), as is related in the exegesis, or for intensification in evil.

ukberi-tibyan:1-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ (١) مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ (٢) وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ (٣) وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ): «مَا» may be in the sense of «الَّذِي» (that which), with the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) omitted, or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).
[On the latter,] «الْخَلْق» is in the sense of «الْمَخْلُوق» (what is created). Or, if you wish, it is in its proper sense, i.e. from the evil of His creating, that is, His bringing into being.
It has also been read «مِنْ شَرٍّ» with tanwīn (nunation); on this, «مَا» is a badal (substitute) for «شَرّ», or redundant (zāʾida). It cannot be negative, because what falls within the scope of the negative «مَا» cannot precede it; for that reason the implied form cannot be «مَا خَلَقَ مِنْ شَرٍّ» (He did not create any evil); moreover, it is corrupt in meaning.
(النَّفَّاثَاتِ) and «النَّافِثَات» have one meaning. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Falaq
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الفَلَقِ﴾ ("Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak"): it is the falaq of the morning, i.e. its light; one also says ”فَرَقُ الصُّبْحِ“, and one says ”هُوَ أبْيَنُ مِن فَلَقِ الصُّبْحِ“ ("it is clearer than the break of morning"). And the meaning of ”اَلْفَلْقُ“ is creation. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فالِقُ الإصْباحِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 96] ("the Cleaver of daybreak") and ﴿فالِقُ الحَبِّ والنَّوى﴾ [al-Anʿām: 95] ("the Cleaver of grain and date-stone"). Likewise He cleaves the earth with vegetation and the clouds with rain. If you reflect on creation, it becomes clear to you that most of His creating is through cleaving open; so al-falaq is all created things, and the break of morning is part of that.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ غاسِقٍ إذا وقَبَ﴾ ("and from the evil of darkness when it settles"): by ”غاسِقٍ“ the night is meant. ﴿إذا وقَبَ﴾: when it enters. The night was called ”غاسِقٌ“ — and Allah knows best — because it is colder than the day, and ”اَلْغاسِقُ“ is the cold.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَمِن شَرِّ النَّفّاثاتِ في العُقَدِ﴾ ("and from the evil of the blowers on knots"): ”اَلنَّفّاثاتُ“ are the sorceresses; they blow (tanfuthu), i.e. they spit without saliva, as if it were blowing, as everyone who performs incantations does.
